name: spec
description: Spec pipeline v7 — a small code program run by a trusted engineer, verified by executed evidence. Full lifecycle: greenfield genesis (/spec:genesis, including an in-driver taste-funnel explore state and design-ratification state) → roadmap briefs → /spec:sketch → /spec:plan → optional /spec:design (mock-bound, deterministic fidelity gates) → /spec:build (direct Sonnet worker dispatch per layer wave, executed red-check) → /spec:review (spec-review-driver.js stepped, driver-stepped: deterministic legs via review-legs.js + ONE fresh-context reviewer whose non-soft findings carry executed repros; verdict derived by verdict.js) → /spec:release, plus /spec:atlas, /spec:status, /spec:doctor, /spec:enforce, /spec:escape, /spec:replay. Changelog (last 3): 7.44.0 — replay mutation authoring moves in-session (direct fix 2026-08-31, amends specs/20260819/02 D10 and specs/20260820/02 D5): /spec:replay Phase 1 step 4 no longer dispatches a mutation-authoring agent — the orchestrating session writes the mutation itself (Edit/Write into the scratch worktree, same marker-guard write path, git still first touched at step 5's pinned capture). The dispatch was refused by hosts' unattended permission layer (salon-os 2026-08-31, three refusals; the 2026-08-23 /private/tmp Edit/Write denial was the same layer one level down), and the delegation carried no measurement value — blindness is a property of the Phase 2 blind-reviewer dispatch, never of who wrote the patch, which is unchanged, as are scoring, recording, teardown, and the corpus. AC-20260820-02-6's pin is rescoped to the renamed 'Author the mutation (D2)' step; review.md's REPLAY step and spec-review-driver.js's prompt now say in-session mutation authoring. 7.43.0 — ci leg honest absence (specs/20260830/03-ci-leg-honest-absence.md): an unpushed commit's per-SHA CI query returned an empty run list, which mapped to `unavailable: "no-adapter"` — indistinguishable from a repo with no CI at all — so the review/release ci leg reported green while origin's branch had been red for days (salon-os 2026-08-30: origin red four days, local main 23 commits ahead, leg CLEAN). `ci-query.js --commit` now falls back, only when the sha is on no remote ref, to its own `--branch` query against the current branch; a found run yields `{shaUnseen:true, branch, branchRun}`, mapped by both legs to an evidence row `{unavailable:"sha-unseen", branch, branchConclusion}` at exit 0 unconditionally (JJ ruling 2026-08-30: report honestly, never block — local work may be exactly what fixes the red). `/spec:review` and `/spec:release` now render one ⚠️ line naming the branch and conclusion when `branchConclusion` is `failure`/`timed_out`/`cancelled`; every other structural-absence path (no gh, no remote, `forge:"none"`, a contained sha with no runs) is byte-identical to before. 7.42.1 — deviations sidecar header is spec-scoped (direct doctrine work, 2026-08-30): the sidecar is per-spec and shared by every worker in a build plus review's own fold, but its header was unspecified, so the first worker to create it improvised one — a layer-titled header (`(tests layer)`) then read to a sibling worker as another run's log and produced a misattributed-provenance return. `/spec:build`'s Worker Contract now prescribes a spec-scoped header only, never a layer or worker name; headers stay inert to the `^- ` ledger count and to the close-time sidecar grammar, so no count, refusal, or fold behavior changes.
